exposure: Hepatitis-E virus (HEV) infection status (Acute Viral Hepatitis-E, Acute Liver Failure-E, non-HEV acute hepatitis, healthy control)
outcome: Plasma untargeted metabolomics (choline, sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine, O-palmitoyl-r-carnitine, taurocholic acid, taurochenodeoxycholic acid)
Cytokine profile (TNF-a, IL-1b, IL-9, IL-22, IL-33, IFN-g, IL-12p70, MIP-1a, fractalkine, SDF-1a)
Immune cell profiling (naive T/B cells, CD4, CD8 Tcm, Tem, plasmablasts)
Maternal complications (eclampsia, disseminated intravascular coagulation, preterm premature rupture of membranes)
cohort: Pregnant women categorized into groups based on HEV infection status and severity (acute viral hepatitis, acute liver failure due to HEV, non-HEV acute hepatitis) and healthy controls.
finding: HEV infection, especially leading to acute liver failure (ALF-E) during pregnancy, causes significant detrimental immunometabolic shifts (e.g., decreased choline/carnitine, increased inflammatory cytokines and bile acids) that contribute to severe adverse obstetric complications, including higher failed inductions, preterm births, and increased maternal and fetal mortality.
mod_finding: Patients with ALF-E showed higher rates of failed inductions.
